title.purpose: Large numeric values — plan prices, stat-tile figures. Tabular-nums.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked labels — stat labels, sidebar section headers.

mono.purpose: Tabular data that must not shift width: call timers, scores.

shadows.name: ambient-interactive

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Violet halo on focused inputs and interactive elements.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action — violet→indigo gradient fill, used once per view for the single most important action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #8b5cf6, #6366f1); color: #fff; border: none; border-radius: 12px; padding: 11px 18px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.9rem; box-shadow: 0 6px 20px -6px #8b5cf6; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 6px 20px -6px #8b5cf6, 0 0 0 3px rgba(139,92,246,0.14); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Neutral bordered button — sits visually behind Primary, no gradient or shadow.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #1c1f2b; color: #eef0f6; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12); border-radius: 12px; padding: 11px 18px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.9rem; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.2); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(139,92,246,0.14); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Recessed (inset) field — background sits one step below canvas, violet ring on focus.
components.css: .ds-input { font: inherit; background: #0c0e15; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12); border-radius: 12px; color: #eef0f6; padding: 11px 13px; width: 100%; transition: border-color 0.2s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #8b5cf6; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(139,92,246,0.14); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #5b6377; }

narrative.overview: HusAI's current visual system is a dark-first (with a fully-designed light counterpart), violet-anchored interface built for a moment of real pressure: a VA on a live call, needing calm, precise help without visual noise. The system leans toward Raycast's control-panel precision and Linear's restraint, layered with a single warm signal color (violet→indigo) that means "this is the brand acting on your behalf," and a second, deliberately rarer color (fuchsia) that means "the AI is live right now." Everything else — text, borders, surfaces — stays neutral so those two signals stand out when they appear. The color palette is now a closed, enforced list (see rules below): every saturated/semantic token is declared under one of four categories (Brand, AI/Live, Semantic status, Neutral) directly in styles.css, with two documented exceptions (a stray gradient in the logo mark, an intentionally always-dark landing-page section). The Once-Per-Page and Two-Signal rules are enforced on the Dashboard and Sidebar. The system is not yet as visually restrained as its Raycast influence suggests it should be on depth and spacing: cards and interactive elements still use soft ambient box-shadows on hover (a glow-and-lift feel) rather than Raycast's shadow-free, pure surface-ladder depth model, and there is no fixed section-rhythm token yet. This is stated plainly as the honest current baseline, not glossed over — it's the most concrete lever available if a future pass wants to move closer to that reference.
keyCharacteristics: Two-signal color language: violet for brand/action, fuchsia strictly for "AI is active right now"
Flat-at-rest, lift-on-interaction elevation (borders do the resting work; shadow is reserved for hover/focus feedback)
Generous fluid spacing driven by clamp(), so density adapts smoothly rather than snapping at breakpoints

A recurring pulsing-dot motif (coach-pulse) is the app's signature "something live is happening" language, reused identically across the LIVE nav badge, the sidebar's active-call status, and the floating coach header

rules.name: The Closed Palette Rule
rules.body: Every saturated/semantic color is declared in styles.css under one of four categories: Brand (violet/indigo), AI/Live (fuchsia), Semantic status (danger/warning only — no success color), Neutral. A new color requires picking a category or adding a documented Known Exception, never silent drift. Pure #fff/#000 are the neutral scale's extremes and aren't tokenized separately.

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule (enforced)
rules.body: Violet = the brand acting. Fuchsia = the AI acting live, right now. Fixed violations: the notification dot (was fuchsia, now violet — it isn't AI-live), coach-status-live (was violet, now fuchsia — it is), and the sidebar LIVE badge (was always-on, now wired to real call state).

rules.name: The Once-Per-Page Rule (implemented on Dashboard/Sidebar)
rules.body: A saturated accent appears at full strength at most once per viewport. The Dashboard hero banner is the sole survivor; the sidebar Start-a-Call button, Pro promo card, header CTA, and Quick Actions tile were demoted to flat accent or neutral. Chart/data-encoding color (trend bars, legend dots) is a separate category, not covered.

rules.name: No Success Color
rules.body: There is deliberately no dedicated success/positive color. A score improving is shown with neutral text plus a directional glyph, never brand violet (fixed: .delta.good was reusing --accent-bright for this).

rules.name: The Zero-Shadow Rule (pinned target, not yet implemented)
rules.body: No element carries a box-shadow for depth, at rest or on interaction — surface-color steps and hairline borders do all the depth work. Focus rings and the live-pulse animation are exempt (state signals, not depth). Supersedes the Rest-Is-Flat Rule's hover-shadow allowance.

rules.name: The Rest-Is-Flat Rule (current, partially superseded)
rules.body: Surfaces carry a border, never a shadow, at rest — this half already matches the pinned target; the hover-shadow half is retired by the Zero-Shadow Rule.

rules.name: The Section-Rhythm Rule (pinned target, not yet implemented)
rules.body: Major page sections are separated by a fixed 96px gap (not fluid) — spacing within a section still scales with --gap. No dedicated section-gap token exists today.

dos: Do treat violet as the only "brand action" color and fuchsia as the only "AI is live" color — never swap their roles.
Do keep cards and rows flat (border only) at rest; add the Ambient Interactive shadow only on hover/focus/floating states.
Do use the uppercase, tracked Label style for section headers and stat labels — it's the app's one consistent all-caps convention.
Do let spacing scale fluidly with clamp() rather than jumping at fixed breakpoints.
Do pick one of the four color categories (or a documented Known Exception) before adding any new saturated color — never drift in a one-off hex.
donts: Don't introduce a third saturated brand color for decoration. Anything that isn't violet, fuchsia, or a strict danger/warning status stays neutral gray.
Don't apply a resting shadow to a card or tile — that's reserved for interaction, per the Rest-Is-Flat Rule.

Don't recolor an icon or status element to violet/fuchsia when its real-world meaning is something else (destructive, warning, success) — semantic color always wins over brand color. (Fixed: .delta.good.)
Don't use the pill/999px radius on anything that isn't a status chip, badge, or toggle.

Don't use a thick (>1px) or full-strength-accent border as a decorative left-edge marker — reserved for genuine typographic conventions (blockquotes) at a subdued weight (2px, --border-accent), never as a card/tab pseudo-selection indicator.
